cover_headline: Anahat Singh Stuns Eight-Time World Champion El Sherbini at Silicon Valley Open
facts: Beat eight-time world champion and top seed Nour El Sherbini 11-8, 11-8, 11-7 in 30 minutes at the Silicon Valley Open in Redwood City
The win put her into the quarter-finals of the $143,500 PSA Gold event — the biggest win of her professional career
In 2026 she became India's first World Junior champion — the first non-Egyptian winner since 2010 — and the first Indian to win a women's singles silver in squash at the Asian Games

quote.text: I grew up watching every single match of hers.
quote.speaker: Anahat Singh

end.headline: Anahat Singh Stuns Eight-Time World Champion El Sherbini at Silicon Valley Open
end.line: The 18-year-old Indian beat top seed and world No. 3 Nour El Sherbini 11-8, 11-8, 11-7 in 30 minutes in Redwood City to reach the quarter-finals of the $143,500 PSA Gold event.
